title: Trade-In Agreements Chargeback Shortfall: Amount Due Today
content:
**Calculation.** On a **Trade-In Agreements** agreement, the amount paid today is the whole shortfall, figured from the agreement's ledger as the value-credited and covering entries less the deduction, lien payoff and distributed-equity entries, taken as a positive amount and never less than none, rounded to the nearest cent.

## Ledger reading

| Entries on the agreement's history | Effect on the ledger balance |
|---|---|
| Value-credited entries | Added |
| Covering entries (customer payments and roll-ins) | Added |
| Value deduction entries (every reason) | Subtracted |
| Lien payoff entries | Subtracted |
| Equity applied to a purchase and equity paid out | Subtracted |

A balance below zero is a shortfall of that size; a balance at or above zero is no shortfall, and nothing is due.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

| Entry | Amount |
|---|---|
| Value credited | $10000.00 |
| Customer payment | $1200.00 |
| Value deductions | $10350.00 |
| Lien payoff | $1200.00 |
| Ledger balance | -$350.00 |
| Amount due today | **$350.00** |

Had the customer payment been $1600.00, the balance would be $50.00 and nothing would be due.
